newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel quiet, seller at three figur.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel quiet, seller at three figur.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was unchanged on Tuesday, with traders saying that crude's recent gains were supporting sellers' higher asking numbers.
Buyers said they were in the $98/$99 region in the quietly talked market and two sellers with 0.7 pct material were seen at $3 to $4 higher.
Better quality material was in the $103/$104 region.
"I am at $98/$99 at present...I certainly would not pay more than $100 at current crude levels," one low sulphur straight-run buyer said. "With crude up the sellers always up their price," he added.
Not too much buying interest was seen from the United States, with a major refiner reported to have bought all it needed recently.
High sulphur Russian M-100 straight run was heard done at two means plus $1, a price described as "not great" for straight run material.
"But then again straight-run margins compared with crude aren't that brilliant," one trader said.
Traders said three M-100 cargoes, loading between June 20 and 25, will be shown soon and may fetch between $1 to $3 premium over two means.
"I think they will not fetch the high price as crude margins have taken a bit of a caning but they are still reasonably good," one trader said.
